title: Choose the security question first
points: CloudTrail records API activity; Config records resource configuration
Inspector finds software vulnerabilities and network exposure
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity; Macie discovers sensitive S3 data
Security Hub prioritizes issues; Detective supplies investigation context
diagram: Independent service tiles grouped by question: activity, configuration, vulnerability, threat, sensitive data, investigation. No sequential arrows between alternatives.
remember: Match the question to its evidence source.

title: Amazon Inspector: coverage before findings
points: EC2: supported packages and network reachability
ECR: supported image OS and application packages
Lambda standard: dependency vulnerabilities; optional code scanning: application code
Coverage status, supported runtimes and exclusions determine what was assessed
diagram: Three resource branches enter Inspector, then findings branch to Security Hub and EventBridge. Scan eligibility is a gate before assessment.
remember: Check coverage before interpreting an empty finding list.

title: EC2 scanning: agent and snapshot paths
points: Agent-based scanning uses Systems Manager inventory on supported instances
Hybrid mode can use EBS snapshots for eligible unmanaged instances
Network reachability analysis is separate from package inventory
Check scan mode, coverage, permissions, exclusions and last scan time
diagram: EC2 has two alternative inventory paths: SSM agent to Inspector, or eligible EBS snapshot to Inspector. Both lead to package findings. Distinct configuration-analysis line for reachability.
remember: Agentless scanning has eligibility and permission requirements.

title: Image and function scans follow the artifact
points: ECR enhanced scanning uses Inspector with repository filters and rescan settings
Lambda standard scans dependencies; code scanning adds supported code checks
Deployment, updates and relevant new vulnerabilities can trigger reassessment
Rebuild or update the artifact, deploy it, then verify the new resource coverage
diagram: Left lifecycle: ECR image digest → scan → rebuild → new digest. Right lifecycle: Lambda code and layers → scan → update → rescan. Independent paths.
remember: Scanning reports risk; your release process delivers the fix.

title: Prioritize and close a vulnerability
points: Combine severity with exploitability, exposure and business impact
Assign owner and remediation deadline; record accepted exceptions
Patch EC2 or rebuild images and functions through controlled deployment
Verify the affected version is gone and the finding state is updated
diagram: Risk inputs feed prioritization, then owner remediation and verification loop. Include finding version and resource identity.
remember: A patched build must reach the running workload.

title: AWS Config records the resource story
points: A recorder captures supported resource configuration and relationships
Recording scope, resource types and Region determine visibility
Config rules evaluate compliance against desired configuration
An aggregator centralizes recorded data; it does not turn on remote recorders
diagram: Resource changes on a horizontal timeline create configuration items in Config; an aggregator receives data from two account/Region boxes.
remember: A central view depends on recording at the source.

title: Configuration history and API history
points: Config history shows what a resource looked like and when it changed
Compliance history shows rule evaluation results over time
CloudTrail supplies recorded API activity for investigation
Correlate resource ID, Region, principal and timestamps before attributing a change
diagram: Aligned rows: configuration state, compliance result and CloudTrail API event. Match times with vertical guides, no claim that every change has a human caller.
remember: Use Config state and CloudTrail activity together.

title: Config rules: managed, Lambda or Guard
points: Managed rules provide AWS-maintained evaluations
Custom Lambda rules implement supported logic in a function
Custom Policy rules use Guard policy language
Scope and trigger settings determine which resources are evaluated
diagram: Three equal alternative rule cards, all point to compliance evaluation. Example desired properties: approved volume type or allowed instance family.
remember: Custom Config rules are not limited to Lambda.

title: Detective and proactive evaluations
points: Detective evaluation checks deployed resource configuration
Triggers can be configuration changes or periodic evaluations, depending on rule
Supported proactive rules evaluate supplied properties before deployment
Evaluation results do not themselves deny an API request
diagram: Left before-deployment resource properties → proactive evaluation result. Right deployed change → detective evaluation result. A separate deployment control gate is clearly labeled separately.
remember: Assessment and enforcement are different controls.

title: Remediate safely with Systems Manager
points: A noncompliant result can start a configured SSM Automation runbook
Grant a scoped execution role and validate current resource state
Use retries, exception handling and approval for disruptive changes
Re-evaluate and retain execution evidence after the change
diagram: Config NON_COMPLIANT → current-state check → SSM Automation → resource change → Config re-evaluation. Failure branch to operator.
remember: Recheck current state before acting on an older evaluation.

title: Logs answer different investigation questions
points: CloudTrail: API activity; Config: configuration history
VPC Flow Logs: network flow metadata, not packet payload
Load balancer, S3 and CloudFront access logs: request evidence
Route 53 public query logs and Resolver query logs cover different DNS paths
diagram: Central investigation case surrounded by six evidence cards. Small destination labels: S3, CloudWatch Logs or Firehose as applicable. No claim all logs support every destination.
remember: Select the needed log type and enable its delivery path.

title: GuardDuty foundational threat detection
points: Analyze CloudTrail management events, VPC flow metadata and DNS activity
Threat intelligence, anomaly detection and behavioral signals create findings
Foundational monitoring uses service data streams without your own trail or flow-log export
This detection path needs no workload agent; Runtime Monitoring is separate
diagram: Three foundational data inputs feed GuardDuty, then a finding card for suspicious API or network behavior. No customer log bucket prerequisite.
remember: Detection data and customer-retained audit logs serve different needs.

title: GuardDuty protection plans extend coverage
points: S3 data access, EKS audit, RDS login and Lambda network activity add signals
Runtime Monitoring uses a security agent for eligible compute workloads
Malware protection examines supported EBS, S3 or backup data paths
Enablement, default settings, Region support and resource coverage must be checked
diagram: GuardDuty center with distinct plan branches: data activity, runtime agent, malware scan. Label optional capabilities; do not depict all plans as agentless.
remember: Verify each protection plan and its resource coverage.

title: Turn a finding into an owned response
points: A finding describes observed suspicious behavior and affected resources
EventBridge can route matching findings to SNS, Lambda or an orchestration workflow
Enrich with resource context; preserve evidence before containment
Approve high-impact actions and verify the result; a finding alone does not block traffic
diagram: GuardDuty finding → EventBridge. Branch to SNS notification and controlled response workflow; workflow includes evidence, approval and containment.
remember: Detection requires a response owner and tested action.

title: GuardDuty across accounts and Regions
points: The management account designates a member as delegated administrator
Trusted access and service permissions enable organization administration
Account enrollment and protection-plan coverage require explicit management
GuardDuty is regional: verify every target account and Region
diagram: Organizations management account designates security account; security account manages members in two Region columns. No implied global activation.
remember: Delegation does not prove complete regional coverage.

title: Security Hub and Security Hub CSPM
points: Security Hub CSPM evaluates controls and security posture
Security Hub correlates security issues to prioritize exposures and response
Findings from services such as Inspector and GuardDuty add context
Enablement and administration differ between the two services
diagram: Two linked panels: CSPM posture findings → Security Hub prioritization; Inspector and GuardDuty also feed Security Hub. Clearly label current service names.
remember: Posture checks and issue prioritization complement each other.

title: CSPM control checks need recording
points: Most AWS CSPM controls use Config rules and resource recording
With both Security Hub and CSPM, a service-linked recorder is created
With CSPM alone, configure the required Config recording yourself
Check account, Region, resource coverage and permissions before trusting results
diagram: Decision split: both services → service-linked recorder; CSPM alone → configure Config recorder. Both lead to control evaluations and findings.
remember: Recording prerequisites depend on the enablement path.

title: Aggregate findings without losing scope
points: Service integrations publish findings with resource and source context
CSPM central configuration and aggregation have distinct roles
Cross-Region aggregation does not enable detection in linked Regions
Track severity, workflow state, owner and evidence links
diagram: Two member accounts in two Regions publish findings to a designated aggregation view. Show enablement required at each source, and a separate administration control line.
remember: An aggregated dashboard is only as complete as its sources.

title: Security automation needs an exit test
points: Filter events by source, finding type and resource scope
Use a scoped role and idempotent actions with retry handling
Require approval for disruptive isolation or access changes
Verify control state, record evidence and route failures to an owner
diagram: Finding → filter → context check → approval where needed → action → verification. Separate failure path to manual handling.
remember: Closing a ticket is not verification of the control.

title: Amazon Detective: investigate relationships
points: Detective organizes activity into behavior graphs and visual context
CloudTrail, VPC flow data and GuardDuty context support investigations
Pivot across principal, IP address, resource and time window
Correlate evidence before deciding the root cause and containment scope
diagram: Behavior graph with principal, IP, EC2 resource and finding connected by labeled observed activity. Time-window selector below; no unsupported accusation labels.
remember: A graph supplies context; an investigator validates the conclusion.

title: Amazon Macie: discover sensitive S3 data
points: Macie inventories supported S3 buckets and discovers sensitive data
Managed identifiers and custom identifiers find selected data patterns
Automated discovery and scoped discovery jobs have different coverage
Findings route through EventBridge and integrations for response
diagram: S3 objects → Macie discovery → sensitive-data finding → EventBridge → controlled response. Show IAM/KMS access gate before content analysis.
remember: Sensitive-data discovery depends on object accessibility and scope.

title: Macie coverage, identifiers and remediation
points: Choose buckets, prefixes, sampling and schedule to fit the question
Validate supported formats, storage classes, encryption and key access
Distinguish bucket policy findings from sensitive-content findings
Restrict exposure through approved S3 and IAM changes, then verify
diagram: Two finding lanes: bucket access posture and sensitive content. Both feed triage; remediation changes S3/IAM, not the classifier itself.
remember: No sensitive-data finding does not prove every object was analyzed.

title: Compare the security evidence services
points: Inspector: vulnerable software or network exposure
GuardDuty: suspicious activity; Macie: sensitive S3 data
Config and CSPM: configuration posture and controls
Detective: investigation; Security Hub: issue prioritization
diagram: Six independent service cards grouped by purpose, with correct official icons and explicit question labels. No pipeline arrows between alternatives.
remember: Combine complementary evidence rather than choosing one universal scanner.

title: Findings and security data for investigation
points: A finding summarizes a detected issue with resource and severity context
Security Lake centralizes supported security logs, events and findings in a data lake
OCSF normalizes supported records; Lake Formation governs subscriber access
Retain CloudTrail and service logs according to your evidence requirements
diagram: Parallel security findings response workflow and Security Lake ingestion of supported logs, events and findings; normalized OCSF records in S3 with authorized subscriber access.
remember: Choose the data product needed for response or investigation.

title: Audit evidence and AWS assurance reports
points: Audit Manager organizes control evidence from supported sources and manual uploads
An assessment report packages selected evidence for review
Artifact provides AWS and eligible third-party assurance reports and agreements
Customer compliance still requires scope, operating procedures and reviewer judgment
diagram: Two distinct folders: customer control evidence via Audit Manager; provider assurance via Artifact. Both support audit review, no certification stamp.
remember: Evidence collection does not certify the workload.

title: Data residency is an end-to-end constraint
points: Select allowed Regions for data, replicas, backups, logs and recovery copies
Map service processing locations, global endpoints and cross-Region integrations
Use policy guardrails plus service configuration and tested transfer controls
Include support access, keys, metadata and third-party processors in the review
diagram: Approved Region boundary contains app, data, logs and backups. Cross-boundary export arrow passes a labeled policy and service-configuration gate to a blocked destination.
remember: A Region condition alone is not a complete residency design.

title: Threat modelling begins at trust boundaries
points: Identify assets, actors, entry points and sensitive data flows
Draw trust boundaries across internet, account, VPC and external service edges
Ask how identity, data integrity, disclosure or availability can fail
Assign mitigations, owners, test cases and residual-risk decisions
diagram: Generic logical data flow: external User to Public API, Worker and Data store inside application account boundary. Worker has separate external vendor API branch. Threats attach to flows; this is not an AWS deployment topology.
remember: Every important boundary needs a threat and a tested mitigation.

title: Work a data-export threat scenario
points: Threat: stolen role credentials read sensitive objects and export data
Prevent: scoped roles, data access policy and approved destination controls
Detect: CloudTrail data events, GuardDuty signals and Macie classification context
Respond: preserve evidence, revoke sessions or restrict access, then validate
diagram: Scenario diagram with role → S3 sensitive data → external destination. Red dashed attempted export and separate prevention, detection and response annotations.
remember: Classification, access prevention and threat detection are separate controls.

title: Least privilege for security automation
points: Read-only investigation and state-changing remediation need different roles
Scope actions to resource tags, accounts and supported resource ARNs
Protect automation against untrusted event fields and confused-deputy paths
Log execution, require approvals where needed and test denied paths
diagram: Two roles: investigator can read evidence; remediator changes only scoped resources. Event validation precedes role assumption and actions.
remember: A response system should not become a new escalation path.

title: Access Analyzer: reason about access
points: External access findings examine supported resource policies and trust
Internal and unused access capabilities answer different permission questions
Validate policies and review public or cross-account exposure
A policy finding does not prove that a principal actually used the access
diagram: Resource policy → Access Analyzer → exposure finding. Separate CloudTrail activity evidence card. Clearly distinguish potential access from recorded use.
remember: Possible access and observed activity require different evidence.

title: AI security evidence and human oversight
points: Record supported model and agent API activity and scoped application telemetry
Protect prompts, outputs, retrieval data and invocation logs as sensitive data
Apply content safeguards, tool permissions and approval for high-impact actions
Correlate security signals with application evidence and data-retention policy
diagram: AI application orchestrator has independent model, authorized retrieval and tool branches. Human approval precedes scoped tool execution; protected audit evidence receives application and tool activity.
remember: Model safeguards do not replace tool authorization or audit evidence.

title: An organization security architecture
points: Delegate security administration and retain workload ownership
Enable regional detection and configuration coverage across accounts
Centralize findings, retain protected logs and route owned responses
Measure coverage, detection, remediation and evidence freshness separately
diagram: Organizations management designates separate delegated security tooling account. Workload findings feed Security Hub and owned response; customer audit logs independently feed protected S3 archive.
remember: Measure coverage as well as finding counts.

title: Walkthrough: Config rule to verified correction
points: Record the target resource and enable a relevant Config rule
Introduce a controlled noncompliant configuration in a lab
Inspect evaluation timestamp and current state before remediation
Run approved Automation, re-evaluate and retain execution evidence
diagram: Five clearly labeled stages: record, evaluate, inspect, remediate, verify. Illustrative compliance transition NON_COMPLIANT → COMPLIANT only after re-evaluation. No fabricated AWS execution claim.
remember: A fresh evaluation must confirm the correction.

title: Walkthrough: Inspector finding to deployed fix
points: Confirm affected resource, package version, scan coverage and exposure
Select a fix or documented mitigation and test it
Patch or rebuild, deploy the corrected artifact, then verify the running version
Review rescan and finding status; retain release and exception evidence
diagram: Illustrative single EC2 package example: vulnerable v1, Inspector finding, approved patch/test, corrected v2, rescan and finding review.
remember: Verify the deployed version rather than only the build result.

title: Walkthrough: investigate suspicious credentials
points: Review finding details, principal, resource, Region and event times
Correlate CloudTrail activity and Detective context with the expected workflow
Preserve evidence and choose proportionate credential or access containment
Check sessions, permissions and workload recovery after response
diagram: GuardDuty finding leads to CloudTrail/Detective evidence correlation and expected-versus-suspicious decision; preserve evidence before controlled containment and validation.
remember: Investigate context before making a disruptive identity change.

title: Walkthrough: sensitive data in an exposed bucket
points: Confirm bucket access posture and Macie discovery scope separately
Review object classification and authorized business access
Restrict unintended access with approved S3/IAM controls
Retest access and classification coverage, preserve evidence and notify the owner
diagram: Two inputs: access-policy evidence and Macie sensitive-data finding merge into triage → approved access correction → denied unauthorized test plus allowed intended access. Illustrative lab only.
remember: Verify both reduced exposure and intended application access.
